title: Black Hole Formation in Failing Core-Collapse Supernovae
source_scope: Over 100 presupernova models studied with the spherically symmetric general-relativistic 1.5D GR1D code and simplified neutrino leakage/heating physics.
physical_quantity: xi_M = (M / M_sun) / (R(M_bary = M) / 1000 km); the paper focuses on xi_2.5 at bounce
locked_external_direction: Higher bounce compactness is associated with faster black-hole formation and progenitors that are harder to explode.
paper_boundary: The source itself treats compactness as a first-order predictor within a stated EOS and simplified 1.5D setup, not a universal one-parameter law.
